input.body:
label: bug
file: src/ingest/parser.ts

The parser splits input only on `"
"` (`text.split("
")`), so CSV files exported with Windows-style CRLF line endings leave a trailing `` character attached to the last field of each row. This corrupts the column count/comparison against the header, triggering the `errors.rowShape` ("Malformed row") error - consistent with the reporter's new accounting tool being run on Windows. The splitting logic in `src/ingest/parser.ts` needs to normalize line endings (e.g. strip `` or split on `/
|
/`) before processing rows.

text: The issue is a classic CRLF line-ending bug: splitting only on `\n` leaves trailing `\r` on each field, causing column count mismatches when Windows-exported files use CRLF.
